programs.formulaSummary: Reduces taxable value before levy-based credits.
programs.application: Apply through local tax officials.

programs.name: Disabled Veteran Homestead Property Tax Credit
programs.ageRule: Qualifying permanent100% service-connected disability, compensated individual unemployability, or eligible survivor.
programs.incomeDefinition: Not income-tested.
programs.maximumBenefit: 100% of qualifying homestead property-tax levy.
programs.formulaSummary: Offsets qualifying taxes on the eligible homestead.
programs.application: File disabled-veteran claim with assessor by July1.
eligibilityNotes: Veteran ownership/occupancy, VA documentation, and surviving-beneficiary rules apply.
For pre-July2026 applications, acreage/appurtenance rules differ from new2026 applications.
interactions: Coordinate credits on the underlying bill; relief cannot exceed eligible taxes.

researchNotes: Owner 2025 claims use 2024 income; renter claim-year2025 uses 2025 income. These are not the same income window.
Levy and prior-tax-liability inputs are necessary for complete owner calculations.

The HHS manual’s $17,000-income example uses 50%, matching its 2024 table, without naming a base year. Its 2025 table lists 70% at that income. Funding, final rounding and specified age-70 source conflicts remain unresolved; this profile does not provide a validated award.

name: Kansas
overview: Kansas offers three mutually exclusive homeowner refund routes, with different income definitions.

programs.name: Homestead Refund (K-40H)
programs.ageRule: Born before January1,1970; or qualifying disability/blindness; or qualifying dependent child.
programs.incomeDefinition: Household income, including 50% of Social Security under K-40H rules.
programs.maximumBenefit: Up to $700.
programs.formulaSummary: Income-table percentage of qualifying property taxes, subject to program cap.
programs.application: File K-40H with Kansas Revenue.
eligibilityNotes: Full-year Kansas residence, owner occupancy, and $350,000 home-value limit.
interactions: Only one of K-40H, K-40PT and K-40SVR per household.
programs.programYear: 2025 property taxes/income; claim normally due April15,2026.

programs.name: SAFESR (K-40PT)
programs.ageRule: Age65+ throughout 2025.
programs.incomeDefinition: SAFESR household-income definition; not the newer K-40SVR KAGI definition.
programs.maximumBenefit: 75% of qualifying taxes actually and timely paid.
programs.formulaSummary: Refunds 75% of eligible homestead property taxes.
programs.application: File K-40PT with Kansas Revenue.
eligibilityNotes: Full-year residence, owner occupancy, and $350,000 home-value limit.
interactions: Mutually exclusive with K-40H and K-40SVR.

programs.name: Seniors and Disabled Veterans Refund (K-40SVR)
programs.ageRule: Qualifying senior age65+, disabled veteran, or eligible surviving spouse.
programs.incomeDefinition: From 2025: total Kansas adjusted gross income of all household members.
programs.maximumBenefit: Qualifying tax increase over the program base year.
programs.formulaSummary: Current eligible homestead tax minus eligible base-year tax.
programs.application: File K-40SVR; establish base-year information.
eligibilityNotes: Full-year Kansas residence and owner occupancy.
Base-year home value cannot exceed $350,000.
interactions: Mutually exclusive with K-40H and K-40PT.
programs.programYear: 2025 current-year taxes/income and applicable historical base year.

researchNotes: Renters are not eligible for these three programs.
K-40SVR changed household income in 2025; K-40H and SAFESR definitions did not change.
Claims can be advanced to pay property taxes, so cash timing can precede filing.

name: Kentucky
overview: The principal statewide residential relief identified is an assessed-value homestead exemption for older or totally disabled owners.

programs.name: Homestead Exemption
programs.ageRule: Age 65+ during the tax period, or qualifying total disability.
programs.incomeDefinition: Not income-tested.
programs.maximumBenefit: $49,100 reduction in assessed value for 2025 and 2026; this is not a $49,100 tax credit.
programs.formulaSummary: Deduct the statutory exempt value from eligible assessed value, then apply property-tax rates.
programs.application: Application and proof to the county Property Valuation Administrator by December 31 of the eligible year.
eligibilityNotes: Own, occupy and maintain the property as a personal residence on January 1.

researchNotes: No statewide renter credit or refundable property-tax circuit breaker was identified in the reviewed DOR materials.
Exemption tax savings require applicable tax rates and are contextual to the credit comparison.

name: Louisiana
overview: Louisiana provides a homestead exemption, an income-tested assessment freeze, and a narrow property-tax bill credit for qualifying dwelling owners who lease the land and are not otherwise entitled to homestead exemption.

programs.name: Homestead Exemption
programs.ageRule: No general age restriction.
programs.incomeDefinition: Not income-tested.
programs.maximumBenefit: $7,500 of assessed value, with tax and property limitations.
programs.formulaSummary: Exempt the eligible assessed-value portion from covered ad valorem taxes.
programs.application: Apply to the local assessing authority.
eligibilityNotes: Bona fide owner-occupied homestead; municipal and other constitutional limitations apply.

programs.name: Special Assessment Level
programs.ageRule: Age 65+ or specified military, disability or surviving-family categories.
programs.incomeDefinition: Prior-year federal AGI under the constitutional rules.
programs.incomeLimits: Statutory income ceiling applies; use the tax-year-specific application threshold.
programs.maximumBenefit: Future eligible assessed-value increases are limited; the amount depends on the frozen assessment and tax rates.
programs.formulaSummary: Freeze qualifying assessed value at the first eligible year while conditions continue.
programs.application: Apply to the local assessing authority.
eligibilityNotes: Property must qualify for the homestead exemption.
An assessment freeze does not freeze tax rates or necessarily the total bill.

programs.name: Residential Lessees’ Property Tax Credit
programs.ageRule: No general age restriction.
programs.incomeDefinition: Not income-tested.
programs.maximumBenefit: Covered tax on $7,500 assessed value or actual covered tax, whichever is less.
programs.formulaSummary: Reduce the qualifying residence's ad valorem tax bill by the lesser of actual covered tax and tax on $7,500 assessed value. This provision does not provide a separate cash payment or income-tax refund.
programs.application: Bill-level credit under R.S. 47:1710; local claim procedures were not established by this source review.
eligibilityNotes: Residential lessee means a person who owns and occupies the residence, including a mobile home, but does not own its land.
Ordinary apartment renters are not eligible through this provision.
Non-entitlement to homestead exemption must be established separately; failing to apply for that exemption does not by itself establish credit eligibility.
Covered residence tax, applicable rates and local parcel facts must be established; unknown facts do not establish a zero award.
interactions: Available only where the claimant is not otherwise entitled to the homestead exemption.
Article VII §20(A)(1) already extends homestead exemption to many owner-occupied primary dwellings on leased land. The remaining eligible claimant population is unresolved.
programs.programYear: 2025 residence ad valorem tax bill; distinct from calendar-year cash payments and the income-tax return.

sources.title: Louisiana Constitution, Article VII §20(A)(1) and (B) — homestead overlap and lessee relief
June 2025 Louisiana Administrative Code, 61:V §101(F)(2), physical page 292

researchNotes: The narrow lessee credit must not be advertised as a general renter credit.
Housing filters classify ownership of the dwelling: a dwelling owner who rents the underlying land appears under homeowners.
Current constitutional pages contain future-effective amendments; a 2025 comparison must use provisions in force for 2025.

R.S. 47:1710 remains in the statute and June 2025 administrative compilation. Act 11 of the 2024 Third Extraordinary Session does not repeal it. Act 12's contingent changes did not become operative after voters rejected the required Article VII amendment on March 29, 2025.

The lessee entry identifies a nonrefundable property-bill offset. Homestead entitlement, remaining eligible claimant scenarios, covered levies and local claim procedures remain unresolved; initial source-pass completion does not validate a household award.

name: Maine
overview: The refundable Property Tax Fairness Credit covers qualifying homeowners and renters, with higher caps for seniors and certain disabled veterans.

programs.name: Property Tax Fairness Credit
programs.ageRule: All ages; higher maximum at age 65 or older.
programs.incomeDefinition: Federal AGI plus statutory additions, including specified nontaxable income and losses; Schedule PTFC/STFC defines adjustments.
programs.incomeLimits: 2025: $63,750 single; $82,500–$101,250 for head-of-household/joint/surviving-spouse filers depending on dependents; $102,500 for eligible seniors.
programs.maximumBenefit: 2025 ordinary cap $1,000 under age 65 or $2,000 age 65+; eligible 100% permanently disabled veterans can receive an additional matching credit, subject to housing-tax expense limits.
programs.formulaSummary: Eligible property taxes or 15% of occupancy rent, capped by the benefit base, minus 4% of program income; then apply the credit cap.
programs.application: File Schedule PTFC/STFC with Form 1040ME, including when filing only to claim refundable credits.
eligibilityNotes: Maine principal residence and resident/part-year resident rules apply.
Married filing separately is ineligible.
Rent allowances require utility and subsidy adjustments.
interactions: The disabled-veteran additional credit cannot raise combined credit above qualifying taxes and rent constituting taxes.

laterChanges: For tax years beginning in 2026, the ordinary under-65 maximum rises to $1,500; the senior maximum remains $2,000. Source: Maine Revenue Services 2026 legislative changes, https://www.maine.gov/revenue/sites/maine.gov.revenue/files/inline-files/legischange26.pdf.
researchNotes: The benefit base limits the housing expenses used in the formula; comparing only headline maximum credits is insufficient.
General homestead exemptions and deferrals are separate property-tax mechanisms.

name: Maryland
overview: Maryland operates separate homeowner and renter circuit-breaker programs with different income thresholds, asset/age rules and application timing.

programs.name: Homeowners’ Property Tax Credit
programs.ageRule: No general minimum age.
programs.incomeDefinition: Combined gross household income, including nontaxable income, with exclusions for specified occupants.
programs.incomeLimits: Gross household income no more than $60,000; net worth excluding the residence and qualifying retirement savings no more than $200,000.
programs.maximumBenefit: Eligible property tax above the statutory income-based limit; eligible assessed value is limited to $300,000.
programs.formulaSummary: Credit eligible tax above a graduated income limit: 0% of first $8,000, 4% of next $4,000, 6.5% of next $4,000, and 9% above $16,000.
programs.application: Apply annually to SDAT; the 2025 application deadline was October 1, 2025.
eligibilityNotes: Legal interest and principal-residence occupancy conditions apply.
2025 application uses calendar-year 2024 income and year-end 2024 assets.
interactions: Eligible taxes reflect the Homestead assessment reduction; fixed water/sewer charges, excess acreage and business portions are excluded.
State, county and municipal Homestead assessment bases can differ. Their aggregation with the Homeowners' $300,000 assessment cap remains unresolved for a general calculation.
programs.programYear: 2025 property-tax credit uses 2024 household income; do not equate the credit year with the income year.

sources.title: 2025 Tax–Property §9-105 — differing State, county and municipal Homestead bases

programs.name: Renters’ Tax Credit
programs.ageRule: Age 60+, fully disabled, or younger renter meeting dependent-child, income and housing conditions.
programs.incomeDefinition: Combined gross household income, including nontaxable retirement income.
programs.incomeLimits: Younger applicants face household-size limits; older/disabled applicants use the rent-to-income calculation. Apply the applicable-year application rules.
programs.formulaSummary: 15% of occupancy rent minus 0% of first $4,000 of income, 2.5% of next $4,000, and 5.5% above $8,000, subject to eligibility and cap.
programs.application: Apply annually to SDAT by October 1 of the application year; payment is a direct state check.
eligibilityNotes: At least six months in a qualifying Maryland principal residence.
Occupancy rent excludes heat, utilities and fees.
Tax-exempt dwellings are excluded; younger applicants have additional subsidy restrictions.

The under-60 route has an unresolved source conflict: statute specifies Census poverty thresholds, while the 2025/2026 forms use HHS poverty guidelines. Exact reference-year and family-composition treatment remain unresolved for eligibility calculations.
programs.programYear: The 2025 application uses 2024 rent and income; the 2026 application uses 2025. Rent year and application/payment year must remain separate.

2026 Renters' Tax Credit application — 2025 rent and income

programs.name: Homestead Property Tax Credit
programs.ageRule: No general age restriction.
programs.incomeDefinition: Not income-tested.
programs.maximumBenefit: Credit on annual taxable-assessment increases above 10% for State property tax, or the local cap of 10% or less.
programs.formulaSummary: Credit the property tax attributable to eligible assessment growth above the applicable cap; market-value assessment itself is not frozen.
programs.application: One-time principal-residence application to SDAT.
eligibilityNotes: Applies to one qualifying principal residence; ownership and occupancy conditions apply.
interactions: This assessment-growth credit is distinct from the income-based Homeowners’ Tax Credit.
Do not count bill relief twice. The income-based Homeowners' Credit uses its statutory Homestead-adjusted assessment basis; aggregation of differing jurisdictional bases remains unresolved.

Homeowner credit is bill relief, so income-tax refundability is not a meaningful classification.

The under-60 renter Census/HHS threshold conflict and the Homeowners' differing-jurisdiction Homestead bases remain unresolved calculation limits. Initial source-pass completion does not certify population eligibility or household amounts.

name: Massachusetts
overview: A refundable senior circuit breaker covers qualifying homeowners and renters; it is distinct from locally administered property-tax exemptions.

programs.name: Senior Circuit Breaker Tax Credit
programs.ageRule: At least one eligible taxpayer must be 65 or older by the end of the tax year.
programs.incomeDefinition: Massachusetts adjusted gross income with statutory additions and subtractions; excludes specified personal exemptions.
programs.incomeLimits: 2025 total income: $75,000 single, $94,000 head of household, $112,000 joint; married filing separately is ineligible.
programs.maximumBenefit: $2,820 for tax year 2025.
programs.formulaSummary: Credit qualifying housing payments above 10% of program income, limited to the annual maximum. Owner expenses include property taxes after reductions and half of separately stated water/sewer charges. Renters use 25% of annual qualifying rent.
programs.application: File Schedule CB with the Massachusetts income-tax return; a return is required even when no tax would otherwise be due.
eligibilityNotes: Principal residence required.
2025 assessed-value ceiling for homeowners is $1,298,000, before residential exemptions and after abatements.
Dependents, nonresidents, subsidized renters and tenants of tax-exempt property are excluded.
interactions: Subtract property-tax abatements, exemptions and other reductions when measuring owner payments.
programs.programYear: Tax year 2025; claimed with the return filed in 2026.

sources.title: 2025 tax tips for seniors and retirees

researchNotes: The legal household income definition differs from federal AGI.
Locally administered exemptions are context, not an additional statewide cash credit. The inventory does not enumerate every municipal option.

name: Michigan
overview: Michigan’s refundable Homestead Property Tax Credit covers homeowners and renters, with alternate senior and disability calculations.

programs.name: Homestead Property Tax Credit
programs.ageRule: All ages, subject to other eligibility rules.
programs.incomeDefinition: Total Household Resources (claimant and spouse), including specified nontaxable income and loss addbacks.
programs.incomeLimits: 2025 THR no more than $71,500; phaseout starts above $62,500.
programs.maximumBenefit: $1,900 for 2025 before applicable phaseout.
programs.formulaSummary: A claimant-specific percentage (generally 60%, with enhanced/alternate senior or disability rules) of qualifying taxes or 23% of rent above 3.2% of THR; apply maximum and income phaseout.
programs.application: File MI-1040CR, with or without an income-tax return. Eligible veterans/blind claimants compare the alternate MI-1040CR-2.
eligibilityNotes: Michigan residence for at least six months.
Owner taxable-value ceiling $165,400 for 2025; no corresponding renter value ceiling.
Use property taxes levied for the year; tax-exempt housing and public-assistance conditions can affect the credit.
interactions: Do not add the veteran/blind alternative to the ordinary credit.
Special rent/service-fee and senior calculations require their own inputs.

researchNotes: Taxable value is not market value or state equalized value.
The Homestead Property Tax Credit is different from the Principal Residence Exemption.

name: Minnesota
overview: Minnesota has separate refundable renter and homeowner programs; the homeowner program includes a special refund for sharp tax increases.

programs.name: Renter’s Credit
programs.ageRule: All ages, subject to other eligibility rules.
programs.incomeDefinition: Federal AGI with prescribed spouse/nonresident adjustments and subtractions for dependents, age/disability, and eligible stipend payments.
programs.formulaSummary: The annual credit table applies income-dependent thresholds, copayments and caps to 17% of qualifying rent; subsidized-rent adjustments may apply.
programs.application: File M1RENT and M1REF with the Minnesota income-tax return; include Certificates of Rent Paid.
eligibilityNotes: A qualifying Minnesota resident renting tax-paying or qualifying payments-in-lieu property.
Mobile-home lot rent alone goes through M1PR, not M1RENT.
interactions: Income-tax filing replaced the separate renter refund starting with 2024 rent.
Do not double count rent between M1RENT and homeowner lot-rent claims.

programs.name: Homeowner’s Homestead Credit Refund — regular
programs.ageRule: All ages, subject to other eligibility rules.
programs.incomeDefinition: 2025 household income under M1PR, with specified dependent, retirement, senior and disability subtractions.
programs.maximumBenefit: Use the revised 2025 M1PR table; a 2026 law increased 2025 refunds by nearly 15%.
programs.formulaSummary: Income-banded thresholds, claimant copayments and maximum refunds apply to qualifying property taxes.
programs.application: File Form M1PR separately from the income-tax return.
eligibilityNotes: Own and occupy the qualifying homestead on January 2, 2026.
Homestead classification and no delinquent property taxes (or qualifying arrangement) required.
interactions: May qualify for both regular and special refunds.
programs.programYear: 2025 household income with property taxes payable in 2026; claim generally filed in 2026.

programs.name: Homestead Credit Refund — special
programs.ageRule: All ages, subject to other eligibility rules.
programs.incomeDefinition: No income limit.
programs.maximumBenefit: $1,000 under the published 2025 instructions; verify against the revised 2025 return before calculation.
programs.formulaSummary: A refund of qualifying increases above the statutory percentage threshold; 2025-to-2026 net tax must rise more than 12% and at least $100, excluding improvements.
programs.application: Claim on Form M1PR.
eligibilityNotes: Must own and occupy the same home January 2, 2025 and January 2, 2026.
interactions: Can accompany a regular refund, subject to M1PR coordination.
programs.programYear: 2025 M1PR compares taxes payable in 2025 and 2026.

laterChanges: A law enacted in May 2026 retroactively increased regular 2025 homeowner refunds. Current-law tax-year-2025 comparisons must use revised tables, not mechanically inflate old model results.
researchNotes: The regular homeowner and renter programs use different income concepts and different housing-tax years.
The annual adjustments PDF showing a $3,480 homeowner maximum predates the one-time 2026 increase; do not use that maximum as current entitlement.

name: Mississippi
overview: Mississippi’s homestead system includes a regular property-tax bill credit and larger age/disability exemptions; it is not a refundable income-based renter circuit breaker.

programs.name: Regular Homestead Exemption — bill credit
programs.ageRule: Ordinary tier for eligible owners under age 65 who do not qualify for the disability tiers.
programs.incomeDefinition: Not income-tested.
programs.maximumBenefit: Up to $300 reduction in taxes under the assessed-value table.
programs.formulaSummary: Apply the regular homestead tax-credit table to eligible assessed value.
programs.application: Apply to the county tax assessor January 1–April 1; reapply after relevant changes.
eligibilityNotes: Own and occupy the principal residence on January 1.
Ownership, head-of-family and state-tax compliance rules apply.
interactions: Age/disability and total-exemption tiers replace the ordinary tier.

programs.name: Age/Disability Homestead Exemption
programs.ageRule: Age 65+ or qualifying total disability as of January 1.
programs.incomeDefinition: Not income-tested.
programs.maximumBenefit: Covered taxes on the first $7,500 assessed value; certain qualifying veterans/survivors receive full exemption.
programs.formulaSummary: Exempt eligible homestead value from covered property taxes under the applicable tier.
programs.application: Apply to the local assessing authority.
eligibilityNotes: Apply proof-of-age or disability requirements.
Current agency guidance contains further value-protection rules; use 2025 law for calculation.

researchNotes: No general statewide renter credit was identified in reviewed DOR materials.
The regular tier is called an exemption but operates as a bill credit; do not treat it as a cash refund.

name: Missouri
overview: A refundable Property Tax Credit covers qualifying seniors, disabled people and certain surviving spouses who own or rent.

programs.name: Property Tax Credit
programs.ageRule: Age 65+, 100% disabled, service-connected 100% disabled veteran, or age 60+ receiving qualifying surviving-spouse benefits.
programs.incomeDefinition: Missouri adjusted income plus specified nontaxable Social Security, pension, assistance and other income; statutory exemptions and offsets apply.
programs.incomeLimits: Renters/part-year owners: $27,200 single or $29,200 combined; full-year owner-occupiers: $30,000 single or $34,000 combined.
programs.maximumBenefit: 2025: $750 renter or $1,100 owner.
programs.formulaSummary: Apply the MO-PTC chart to program net income and eligible property tax or 20% of qualifying rent; caps and owner/renter income offsets differ.
programs.application: MO-PTS with MO-1040 if an income return is required; otherwise standalone MO-PTC.
eligibilityNotes: Full-year Missouri residence is required for the ordinary age-65 route.
Rental property must pay real-estate tax.
Claim only qualifying principal-residence taxes; fees and excess acreage are excluded.
interactions: County-option senior property-tax freeze relief is a separate local program.

researchNotes: The chart, not a simple maximum-credit comparison, determines the payable amount.
The 2025 MO-CRP instructions confirm the 20% rent conversion after qualifying rent reductions.

name: Montana
overview: Montana combines a refundable elderly homeowner/renter credit with separate property-tax assistance and a time-limited homeowner rebate.

programs.name: Elderly Homeowner/Renter Credit
programs.ageRule: Age 62 or older by December 31, 2025.
programs.incomeDefinition: Gross income of all household members, including specified nontaxable sources; a $12,600 exclusion and income multipliers enter the formula.
programs.maximumBenefit: $1,150 before the gross-income credit multiplier.
programs.formulaSummary: Qualifying billed property taxes plus 15% of rent, less calculated household-income contribution; cap preliminary credit, then apply the gross-income multiplier.
programs.application: Schedule 2EC with Form 2, including when filing only for the refundable credit.
eligibilityNotes: Montana residence at least nine months and qualifying occupancy at least six months.
Only one household member may claim.

programs.name: 2025 Property Tax Rebate for Homeowners
programs.ageRule: No age restriction stated.
programs.incomeDefinition: No income test stated.
programs.maximumBenefit: Up to $400 for the 2025 application program.
programs.formulaSummary: One-time rebate limited by qualifying tax and the program cap; statutory tax-year/payment-year treatment must be checked against the rebate claim.
programs.application: Application window August 15–October 1, 2025.
eligibilityNotes: Owned and occupied principal residence for at least seven months in 2024.
Entity ownership exclusions apply.
programs.programYear: Payment/application program in 2025 with 2024 occupancy; not a recurring 2025 income-tax credit.

programs.name: Property Tax Assistance Program (PTAP)
programs.ageRule: No general age restriction.
programs.incomeDefinition: Prior reference-year federal AGI under the 2025 application rules.
programs.incomeLimits: July 2025 legislative summary lists maximum 2023 FAGI of $28,329 single or $37,968 married/head of household.
programs.maximumBenefit: Reduce taxable value on up to $350,000 of market value to 20%, 50%, or 70%, depending on income.
programs.formulaSummary: Income-tiered reduction of taxable homestead value rather than a refundable renter credit.
programs.application: Apply to Montana DOR under the applicable PTAP-year process.
eligibilityNotes: Ownership and occupancy for at least seven months of the year.
interactions: Separate from the Elderly Homeowner/Renter Credit and one-time homeowner rebate.
programs.programYear: 2025 program description uses 2023 FAGI; do not substitute the current 2027 application’s 2025-income thresholds.

sources.title: Montana Legislature property-tax overview, July 2025, page 8

laterChanges: Homestead and long-term-rental reduced property-tax rates apply in 2026 under separate property-classification reforms; they are not renter cash credits.
researchNotes: The agency overview labels the rebate as 2025 but uses 2024 occupancy. Verify the claim’s tax-payment reference before including it in a tax-year-2025 total.
PTAP and disabled-veteran rate reductions are separate from refundable income-tax credits.

name: Nebraska
overview: Nebraska combines a refundable community-college property-tax credit with property-tax statement credits and a targeted homestead exemption.

programs.name: Community College Property Tax Credit
programs.ageRule: No age restriction.
programs.incomeDefinition: No income test.
programs.maximumBenefit: Qualifying community-college property taxes paid, as computed from parcel records.
programs.formulaSummary: Use Form PTC and DOR parcel lookup for qualifying community-college taxes paid in 2025; excluded levies and existing property-tax credits reduce the eligible base.
programs.application: Form PTC with a Nebraska income-tax return; an amended PTCX is available for missed credits.
eligibilityNotes: Eligibility follows actual payment to the county treasurer.
A lessee paying the county directly may qualify; ordinary rent alone is not sufficient.
interactions: Do not count school-district taxes as an income-tax PTC credit after the 2024 change.
School-district relief now appears on property-tax statements.
programs.programYear: 2025 income-tax credit for qualifying community-college property taxes paid during 2025, usually levied for 2024.

programs.name: Homestead Exemption
programs.ageRule: Qualifying older, disabled and veteran categories; category-specific conditions apply.
programs.incomeDefinition: Application-year household-income schedule.
programs.incomeLimits: Varies by category, filing status and annual table.
programs.maximumBenefit: Partial or full eligible-value exemption; county-average value and statutory limits apply.
programs.formulaSummary: Reduce taxable homestead value under the qualifying category and income/value tables.
programs.application: Form 458 and required income/disability documentation to the county assessor.
programs.programYear: 2025 exemption application rules and 2025 income tables.

programs.name: Real Property Tax Credit
programs.ageRule: No general age restriction.
programs.incomeDefinition: Not income-tested.
programs.maximumBenefit: Varies with qualifying property and tax bill.
programs.formulaSummary: Allocate State funding using parcel credit-allocation valuation and the published annual rate; show credit separately on the property-tax statement.
programs.application: Applied through county assessment and treasury administration.
eligibilityNotes: All taxable real-property parcels generally qualify; land classification affects allocation.
interactions: Applied after homestead exemption, before the School District Property Tax Relief Credit.
Already lowers the amount due; do not add it to relief when the user supplied a net tax bill.

programs.name: School District Property Tax Relief Credit
programs.ageRule: No general age restriction.
programs.incomeDefinition: Not income-tested.
programs.maximumBenefit: Varies with qualifying property and tax bill.
programs.formulaSummary: Apply the State-funded school-district relief calculation to eligible parcel school taxes and display it as a credit on the tax statement.
programs.application: Applied through county property-tax administration.
eligibilityNotes: Use the tax-year-specific published calculation and qualifying school levies.
interactions: Coordinates with homestead exemption and the Real Property Tax Credit.
Separate from the refundable community-college income-tax credit.
Do not add to an already-net property-tax bill.

No direct renter credit was identified.

name: Nevada
overview: Nevada’s residential property-tax abatement limits tax-bill growth. It is distinct from a refundable household credit.

programs.name: Residential Property Tax Partial Abatement
programs.ageRule: No general age restriction.
programs.incomeDefinition: Not income-tested.
programs.maximumBenefit: Tax-bill-growth protection; generally 3% for a qualifying principal residence, with statutory exceptions.
programs.formulaSummary: Abate qualifying tax above the statutory increase cap relative to the prior bill. The cap applies to taxes, not the assessed valuation.
programs.application: Principal-residence or qualifying-rental declarations through the county assessor.
eligibilityNotes: Certain rental property qualifies under rent limits, but the benefit is to the taxed property owner.
New improvements and changes in use can affect the calculation.

researchNotes: No statewide refundable renter credit or income-based circuit-breaker credit was identified in the reviewed Department of Taxation materials.
Veteran, surviving-spouse, disability and other property exemptions are separate context; county-specific tax rates are not estimated.

name: New Hampshire
overview: Income-tested relief refunds part of the State Education Property Tax to qualifying homeowners; local exemptions are separate.

programs.name: Low and Moderate Income Homeowners Property Tax Relief
programs.ageRule: No age restriction stated.

programs.maximumBenefit: Income-tiered relief on qualifying homestead value, capped at $220,000 of value.

name: New Jersey
overview: New Jersey combines ANCHOR, Senior Freeze and Stay NJ with an alternative income-tax property deduction or refundable credit. Benefits require explicit timing and overlap rules.

programs.name: ANCHOR
programs.ageRule: All ages; renter amount increases at age 65.
programs.incomeDefinition: 2025 NJ-1040 line 29 income, with application instructions for nonfilers.
programs.incomeLimits: Owners up to $250,000; renters up to $150,000.
programs.maximumBenefit: 2025-benefit table: homeowners $1,500 at income ≤ $150,000, $1,000 above that to $250,000; renters $450 under 65 or $700 age 65+.
programs.formulaSummary: Fixed income/tenure tiers rather than a tax-to-income threshold.
programs.application: ANCHOR application or combined PAS-1 where required; eligible groups may be automatically enrolled.
eligibilityNotes: Qualifying principal residence on October 1, 2025.
Ordinary rental housing generally must be property-tax subject; specific PILOT rules differ for renters and owners.
interactions: Senior nonfilers’ unclaimed $50 income-tax property credit may be added to payment; do not count twice.
Owner benefits coordinate with Senior Freeze, Stay NJ and other covered property relief.

programs.incomeLimits: 2024 income ≤ $168,268 and 2025 income ≤ $172,475; limited base-year retention exception applies.

name: New Mexico
overview: A statewide refundable senior property-tax rebate covers owners and renters. A separate county-option rebate covers qualifying owners in participating counties.

programs.ageRule: Age 65+ at year-end.

name: New York
overview: New York offers a small refundable low-income owner/renter credit and separate Basic/Enhanced STAR school-property-tax relief.

programs.name: Real Property Tax Credit
programs.ageRule: All ages; higher schedule if claimant, spouse or a claimed dependent is 65+.
programs.incomeDefinition: Federal adjusted gross income starting in tax year 2025, replacing the prior household-income basis.

All owned real-property market value must not exceed $85,000.
Qualifying renters face a $450 average-monthly occupancy-rent ceiling.
Residence must not be fully property-tax exempt.

programs.name: Basic and Enhanced STAR Credit
programs.ageRule: Basic has no age restriction; Enhanced generally requires age 65+, with spouse/sibling and survivor exceptions.

programs.incomeLimits: 2025 Basic credit income limit $500,000; Enhanced income limit $107,300. Legacy Basic exemption limit $250,000.

name: North Carolina
overview: North Carolina’s named circuit breaker is a tax deferral with repayment conditions. Separate elderly/disabled and disabled-veteran exclusions reduce taxable value.

programs.name: Circuit Breaker Tax Deferment Program
programs.ageRule: Age 65+ or qualifying total permanent disability.

programs.formulaSummary: Exclude the statutory portion of permanent-residence value from taxation.
programs.application: AV-9 to county assessor, generally by June 1.

researchNotes: The circuit breaker must not be counted as an outright credit or cash transfer.

programs.name: Property Tax Refund for Elderly and Disabled Persons (2025 application cycle; repealed July 1, 2026)
programs.ageRule: Senior or qualifying disability.
programs.incomeDefinition: Historical program household income includes specified nontaxable receipts and an up-to-$400 deduction for principal-residence property taxes payable in the application year; federal adjusted gross income alone does not establish this amount.
programs.incomeLimits: 2025 application cycle: program household income up to $16,566 for a single-member household or $22,484 for a multiple-member household. These are not the 2026 sales-refund limits.
programs.maximumBenefit: Historical schedule up to 35% of qualified property tax for a single-member household or 55% for a multiple-member household, subject to annual appropriation and proration. No validated dollar entitlement is supplied.

programs.application: Historical 2025 cycle: May 1–July 1, 2025. The advertised 2026 cycle offers sales-tax refunds; it does not advertise an ongoing property-tax application.
eligibilityNotes: For the historical 2025 cycle, the homeowner must have owned the residence for at least three years or have been a South Dakota resident for at least five years.
The 2025 announcement uses 2024 residency, age/disability and income facts. The historical record does not certify every transitional 2026 property claim.
interactions: Revenue pays the larger eligible sales-tax or property-tax refund once; the two awards are not additive.
programs.programYear: 2025 application cycle; 2024 reference taxes/facts. Chapter 10-18A was repealed July 1, 2026. Transitional 2026 property-claim rights and the precise assessment/payable-year mapping are not certified.

sources.title: SDCL 2-14-16: default effective date of legislative acts
SDCL 10-21-4: property-tax due date after assessment and levy

laterChanges: The governor signed 2026 SB 21, enacted as chapter 37, on March 4, 2026. Its repeal of property-refund chapter 10-18A took effect July 1, 2026 under the default effective-date law.

The advertised 2026 application cycle refunds 2025 sales tax. It uses program household-income limits of $17,215 for a single-member household or $23,265 for a multiple-member household, with appropriation-based pro-rata awards capped at $500 or $1,000 respectively. These sales-tax refunds are outside the property/renter-credit comparison.
2026 assessment-freeze income/value thresholds and residency rules differ from 2025 applications.
researchNotes: The identified historical property-refund record covers the 2025 application cycle. Initial source-pass completion does not validate a household award or adjudicate all transitional claims.

SDCL 2-14-18 generally preserves liabilities incurred before repeal unless the repealing act expressly provides otherwise. SB 21 has no specific accrued-claim transition clause; these sources do not settle whether a particular pre-repeal 2026 property claim was an incurred liability.

The historical statute defines tax year as assessment and levy year, while SDCL 10-21-4 makes taxes due January 1 of the following year. The 2025 announcement describes previous-year 2024 taxes/facts; the original claim form and exact assessment/payable-year mapping remain unverified.

The current senior/disability sales-tax refund is separate from the historical property-tax refund. A property-tax or rent deduction in its income test does not make it a property/renter reimbursement.

name: Texas

programs.ageRule: 65 or older, or qualifying disability.

programs.formulaSummary: Localities may exempt taxes, defer them, or limit increases; relief is not uniform statewide.

Ownership interests and jointly owned property affect proration.

name: Wisconsin
overview: Wisconsin combines refundable homestead relief, a nonrefundable income-tax property/rent credit, veteran refunds and several separate property-bill credits.

programs.name: Homestead Credit
programs.ageRule: 18 or older; positive earned income, disability, or claimant/spouse age 62 or older also required.
programs.incomeDefinition: Broad taxable/nontaxable household income, loss/depreciation adjustments and $500 qualifying-dependent deduction.
programs.formulaSummary: Income-adjusted credit based on allowable assessed property taxes or rent constituting property taxes; rent share depends on heat inclusion.
programs.application: File Schedule H or H-EZ with tax bill/rent certificate; most 2025 claims due April 15, 2030.
eligibilityNotes: Full-year Wisconsin resident.
Public assistance and tax-exempt housing can affect allowance.
interactions: The claimant or spouse cannot claim Homestead credit if either claims the veterans/surviving-spouses property-tax credit or farmland preservation credit for the same taxable year.

programs.name: School Property Tax Credit
programs.ageRule: No general age restriction.
programs.incomeDefinition: See program rules.
programs.maximumBenefit: $300, limited by income-tax liability.
programs.formulaSummary: Income-tax credit based on eligible property taxes or rent; owner and renter amounts are combined subject to one cap, with rent table depending on heat inclusion.
programs.application: Claim Form 1 line 16 using 2025 tables.
eligibilityNotes: Uses taxes paid in 2025, unlike Homestead's assessed-tax basis.
interactions: The claimant or spouse cannot claim School Property Tax Credit if either claims the veterans/surviving-spouses property-tax credit for the same taxable year.

programs.name: Veterans and Surviving Spouses Property Tax Credit
programs.ageRule: WDVA-certified eligible veteran or unremarried surviving spouse.
programs.incomeDefinition: See program rules.
programs.maximumBenefit: Eligible property taxes paid on principal dwelling and up to one acre.
programs.formulaSummary: Refunds qualifying paid property taxes; excludes special assessments, interest, service charges and business-use taxes.
programs.application: Obtain WDVA certification and claim through income-tax return.
eligibilityNotes: An otherwise qualified renter may claim actual property taxes required by a written landlord agreement and paid directly to the municipality. Ordinary rent is not a percentage-based tax proxy.
interactions: The claimant or spouse cannot claim School Property Tax, Homestead or farmland preservation credits for the same taxable year when claiming this veterans credit.

name: Wyoming
overview: Wyoming offers an income- and asset-tested homeowner tax refund alongside value exemptions introduced or expanded for 2025.

programs.name: Property Tax Refund Program
programs.ageRule: No general age restriction.
programs.incomeDefinition: Total household income compared with the greater of county or state median household income.
programs.incomeLimits: Up to 145% of applicable median income, with lower benefits above the 125% tier.
programs.maximumBenefit: 75% of eligible taxes paid, limited to half the county median residential tax bill; upper income tier receives a 35% reduction.
programs.formulaSummary: Income-tier refund using paid taxes, county median tax cap and asset/residency tests.
programs.application: Annual application through Department of Revenue or official refund portal; supporting tax-payment and household-income records required.
eligibilityNotes: Wyoming resident at least five years; primary residence.
For 2025, combined countable household assets must not exceed $169,866 times the number of adult household members, with program exclusions.
The asset test is waived when the person's tax liability is strictly greater than 10% of household income; equality does not trigger the waiver.
